Ambiguities.Ambiguity: docs/knowledge-graph.xml lists M-BLOC-TELEMETRY and M-BLOC-SPORT, but no telemetry or sport BLoC exists in the code: telemetry state is a ChangeNotifier service and sport state is a ChangeNotifier repository. The only BLoC in the app is the throttle/brake graph. Mapped to M-SERVICE-TELEMETRY/M-REPO-SPORT plus M-BLOC-THROTTLE-BRAKE and recorded here rather than invented.

The legacy plan split telemetry UI into M-WIDGET-GAUGES, M-WIDGET-TIRES, M-WIDGET-GRAPH and M-WIDGET-DASHBOARD; the repository keeps a single lib/widgets/telemetry/ vertical, so all four collapse into M-WIDGET-TELEMETRY. Splitting it later is a normal change, not a migration decision.

The legacy verification markers ([TelemetryService] …, [SportRepository] …, [TelemetryBloc] State updated) do not match the code: repositories log with debugPrint('SportRepository: …') and telemetry still uses bare print() with no prefix. Markers in the migrated entries use the real text; the telemetry prefix gap is a code clean-up, not a migration task.
The GRACE 3 example referenced test/services/telemetry_service_test.dart, which does not exist. V-M-SERVICE-TELEMETRY therefore has scenarios and markers but no test file.

The grace-explainer reference unique-tag-convention.md shows module anchors with NAME/TYPE attributes, while the 4.2.1 linter rejects attributes on semantic anchors. The linter was treated as authoritative: anchors are bare and the type is written at the start of each Summary.

The legacy inventory covered only telemetry, sport, DI, router and theme. The graph additionally contains car dealer, GT Auto, PSN auth, tracks, shell/navbar, wishlist and the profile feature, because a projection that omits half of the app is not useful. These are additions beyond the legacy inventory, not legacy-derived.

UnsupportedStructures.Unsupported: The packet template (module-id, contract-excerpt, verification-excerpt, assumptions) has no GRACE 4 equivalent; execution context now lives in GraceChangePlan.

ExecutionPolicy (controller-owns / worker-owns / max-fix-attempts-per-step / replan-trigger / checkpoint-requirement) is GRACE 3 orchestration policy; GRACE 4 encodes this per change plan, so it was dropped rather than copied.
FailurePackets template (expected-fields list) is superseded by the plan/assertion model.
